newsitem.title: CHINA: China state purchase of cotton seen down in 1996.
newsitem.headline: China state purchase of cotton seen down in 1996.

text.p: China's state purchase of domestic cotton is expected to slip to 3.0 million tonnes in 1996 from 3.5 million tonnes in 1995, an official said on Thursday.

Low state-set prices had forced farmers to plant other crops, an official of the All China Federation of Supplying and Marketing Cooperative told Reuters by telephone. The federation buys cotton from farmers on behalf of the government.
The state has bought more than 2.4 million tonnes of cotton so far and was expected to buy 3.0 million tonnes in total, the official said.
The official declined to give further details.
China's official forecast for the 1996 cotton harvest was 3.5 million tonnes, down by more than 1.0 million tonnes from 1995 because of low state-set prices.
